checks.label: Backup Enabled (Cloud / ADB)
checks.command: V=$(settings get secure backup_enabled 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$V" ] || [ "$V" = "null" ] && V=$(settings get global backup_enabled 2>/dev/null); echo "$V"
checks.description: Auto-backup (cloud and ADB) can extract sensitive app data. Should be disabled (0) or unset on devices handling sensitive data. Probes both the secure and global namespaces because OEM builds differ on where backup_enabled lives.
checks.remediation: Disable backup via 'settings put secure backup_enabled 0' or enforce a device policy blocking backup. Exclude sensitive apps from auto-backup in their manifest.

checks.label: Auto Backup Enabled
checks.description: Auto backup/restore status
checks.remediation: Review auto-restore settings and disable if not required by your backup policy.

checks.label: Backup Transport
checks.description: Backup transport service
checks.remediation: Verify the backup transport is a trusted service. Replace with a known-good transport if unexpected.

checks.label: Cloud Backup Account
checks.description: Backup manager configuration
checks.remediation: Audit backup manager config and ensure only authorized accounts are used for cloud backup.

checks.label: Mount Points (rw/ro)
checks.description: Review mounted partitions and access permissions (evidence collector)
checks.remediation: Remount sensitive partitions as read-only using 'mount -o remount,ro <partition>'.

checks.label: tmpfs Usage
checks.description: Shows use of temporary memory file system
checks.remediation: Review tmpfs mounts for unexpected entries. Remove unneeded tmpfs mounts to reduce attack surface.

checks.label: World-Readable Files Count
checks.description: World-readable files in /data (top 4 levels). Some are normal; large counts may indicate misconfigured permissions.
checks.remediation: Run 'chmod o-r' on files that should not be world-readable. Audit listed files for sensitive content.

checks.label: World-Readable Files List
checks.description: World-readable files in /data (evidence collector - review for sensitive files).
checks.remediation: Remove world-readable permission from sensitive files using 'chmod o-r <file>'.

checks.label: SQLite DB Permissions
checks.description: SQLite databases should not be world-readable/writable
checks.remediation: Set database permissions to 600 using 'chmod 600 <db_file>' to restrict access to the owning app.

checks.label: Custom Partitions
checks.description: Device partitions - review for sensitive data partitions
checks.remediation: Verify all partitions are expected. Investigate unknown partitions for unauthorized data storage.

checks.label: Mounted Filesystems
checks.description: Mounted filesystems and permissions
checks.remediation: Review mounted filesystems for unexpected entries. Unmount unauthorized mounts and remount as read-only.

checks.label: Writable System Partition
checks.description: Detects the /system partition mounted read-write, which allows firmware modification. The mount point is matched with surrounding spaces so it cannot also match /system_ext, /system/vendor or any other path containing the string. The earlier version grepped for '/system' unanchored, so a writable /system_ext was reported here as a writable /system, producing a second critical finding for a partition that was actually read-only and duplicating the dedicated System_ext check.
checks.remediation: Remount read-only with 'mount -o remount,ro /system' and investigate why it was writable. On a production build /system should never be mounted rw.

checks.label: Vendor Partition Writable
checks.description: Detects the /vendor partition mounted read-write. The mount point is matched with surrounding spaces so it cannot also match /vendor_dlkm, /vendor/odm or any other path containing the string, which the earlier unanchored grep did.
checks.remediation: Remount read-only with 'mount -o remount,ro /vendor' and check for unauthorised modification.

checks.label: World-Writable Files
checks.command: N=$(find /data -maxdepth 4 -type f -perm -o+w | wc -l); echo "count=$N"; find /data -maxdepth 4 -type f -perm -o+w 2>/dev/null | head -10
checks.description: Unprotected sensitive files (scans top 4 levels of /data)
checks.remediation: Remove world-writable permission using 'chmod o-w' on affected files to prevent unauthorized writes.

checks.label: BusyBox Present
checks.description: BusyBox utilities available
checks.remediation: Remove BusyBox if not required. Its rich toolset can aid attackers on compromised devices.

checks.label: Custom Init Scripts
checks.description: Custom init scripts - review for backdoors
checks.remediation: Audit each init script for unauthorized commands. Remove or disable any unrecognized scripts.

checks.label: Recovery Partition Access
checks.command: P=$(ls -d /dev/block/by-name/recovery /dev/block/bootdevice/by-name/recovery 2>/dev/null); if [ -n "$P" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$P"; elif ls -d /dev/block/by-name/recovery /dev/block/bootdevice/by-name/recovery 2>&1 | grep -qi 'permission denied'; then echo UNMEASURED; else echo "ABSENT no recovery partition (A/B device)"; fi
checks.description: Recovery partition accessible
checks.remediation: Restrict access to recovery partition block devices. Ensure only privileged processes can read them.

checks.label: Firmware Version Info
checks.command: getprop ro.build.display.id; getprop ro.build.version.incremental; getprop ro.vendor.build.fingerprint 2>/dev/null | head -3
checks.description: Firmware version information
checks.remediation: Ensure firmware is up to date. Apply the latest OTA or vendor security patch if outdated.

checks.label: OTA Package Location
checks.description: OTA update packages found
checks.remediation: Verify OTA packages are signed by the vendor. Delete stale or unverified update files.

checks.label: Hidden or Extra Partitions
checks.description: Block devices that are not a recognised storage, RAM, loop or device-mapper node. The exclusion covers UFS multi-LUN devices (sda through sdz), eMMC (mmcblkN), and the virtual ram/loop/dm/zram devices every Android kernel creates, so only a genuinely unexpected entry is reported.
checks.remediation: Investigate unexpected partitions for hidden data or unauthorized storage areas.

checks.label: SDCard Mount RW
checks.description: SDCard should not be mounted read-write in restricted environments
checks.remediation: Remount SDCard as read-only or remove it. Enforce a policy blocking external writable storage.

checks.label: Orphaned Files in /data
checks.description: Looks for files owned by root but not by 'system' user (top 3 levels)
checks.remediation: Reassign orphaned files to the correct owner or remove them if they are not needed.

checks.label: External Storage Encryption
checks.command: V=$(getprop ro.crypto.volume.filenames_mode 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$V" ] && echo "UNMEASURED ro.crypto.volume.filenames_mode unset" || printf '%s\n' "$V"
checks.description: External storage filenames should be encrypted
checks.remediation: Enable file-based encryption for external storage. Set ro.crypto.volume.filenames_mode to aes-256-cts.

checks.label: Swap Partition Active
checks.description: Active swap partitions can expose sensitive data (encryption keys, passwords, session tokens) to persistent storage and forensic recovery.
checks.remediation: Disable swap using 'swapoff -a'. If swap is required, ensure the swap partition is encrypted.

checks.label: Storage Chip Identity (UFS/eMMC)
checks.command:
O=''; for d in /sys/block/sd*/device /sys/class/mmc_host/mmc*/mmc*:*; do [ -d "$d" ] || continue; v=$(cat "$d/vendor" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' '); m=$(cat "$d/model" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' '); n=$(cat "$d/name" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' '); r=$(cat "$d/rev" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' '); f=$(cat "$d/fwrev" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' '); [ -n "$v$m$n" ] && O="$O${v:-?}/${m:-$n} rev=${r:-$f}
"; done; if [ -z "$O" ]; then echo 'UNMEASURED no storage device identity readable'; else printf '%b' "$O" | sort -u; fi
checks.description: Manufacturer and part number of the UFS or eMMC device, read from sysfs. Identifies the actual flash silicon without physical access. Useful for forensic provenance: a part number that does not match the expected build is evidence of a swapped or refurbished storage device.
checks.remediation: No action. Record with the audit and compare against the expected part for this hardware revision.
checks.why: Flash part identity is provenance evidence obtainable without opening the device.
checks.risk_if_fail: A substituted storage device goes unnoticed.

checks.label: Storage Wear and End-of-Life State
checks.command:
O=''; for f in /sys/devices/platform/soc/*.ufshc/health_descriptor/eol_info /sys/devices/platform/soc/*.ufshc/health_descriptor/life_time_estimation_a /sys/devices/platform/soc/*.ufshc/health_descriptor/life_time_estimation_b /sys/class/mmc_host/mmc*/mmc*:*/life_time /sys/class/mmc_host/mmc*/mmc*:*/pre_eol_info; do [ -r "$f" ] && O="$O$(basename $f)=$(cat $f 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ')
"; done; if [ -z "$O" ]; then echo 'NOT_OBSERVABLE no UFS/eMMC health descriptor exposed'; else printf '%b' "$O"; fi
checks.description: UFS/eMMC wear indicators. eol_info 0x01 is normal, 0x02 is warning, 0x03 is urgent and 0x04 means the device is at end of life. life_time_estimation values step in 10 percent increments of rated write endurance. Heavy wear on a device that should be lightly used is an indicator of prior use or of unexpected write activity.
checks.remediation: Investigate any eol_info of 0x03 or higher, or a life_time estimate far above what the deployment age would explain. Plan replacement before the flash becomes read-only.
checks.why: Wear state is provenance and reliability evidence readable without physical access.
checks.risk_if_fail: A worn or previously-used flash device is deployed as if new.
